criteria.scenario: A production database has a notifications table around 1 GB, a 512 MB InnoDB buffer pool and growing operational tables. A report query is reported as 'slow', but there is no captured p95, query plan, workload or dataset slice for the complaint.
criteria.decision_to_make: Define the performance investigation and budget before tuning.
must_do: define user/business scenario and measurable budget
capture baseline and representative workload/data
inspect query plans/waits/resource signals
optimize the measured bottleneck
record trade-offs/capacity assumptions
must_not_do: declare a specific index or memory increase correct without evidence

criteria.scenario: Staging is deployed from a Docker image tagged with the commit, but some frontend build flags are injected through Docker ARG/ENV and a developer can rebuild a different image from the same branch before production. Database migration files are in the repo.
criteria.decision_to_make: Define artifact provenance, gate chain and migration/config handling.
must_do: build once and promote the same immutable artifact where possible
record commit/build/artifact digest
distinguish build-time config from secrets/runtime config
include migration compatibility/gates
retain evidence of skipped/failed/retried checks
must_not_do: rebuild different bytes for production and call them verified

criteria.scenario: A release includes migration 0027 and a hierarchy synchronization job. Staging is healthy. Production rollout would affect all institutions at once, and rollback is unclear if the migration writes new derived state.
criteria.decision_to_make: Choose rollout/preflight/health/recovery criteria proportional to data risk.
must_do: verify exact artifact and migration state
assess rollback versus forward-fix after data change
use staged exposure or another blast-radius control where feasible
define smoke/telemetry pause thresholds
record stable-state evidence after observation
must_not_do: equate green CI with production safety
promise rollback without checking data reversibility
declare success immediately after container health turns green

criteria.scenario: A worker claims outbox rows with a two-minute lease, calls an SMS provider outside the transaction and retries failures up to four times. Operators currently see only aggregate 'worker OK' health and cannot tell whether rows are stuck, duplicated or permanently failing.
criteria.decision_to_make: Define SLI/telemetry/alerts that make notification delivery failure diagnosable and actionable.
must_do: instrument outbox/notification state transitions and lease age
correlate job/notification/provider attempts
define actionable stuck/failure alerts and owner
avoid logging sensitive message content unnecessarily
distinguish service liveness from user-visible delivery capability
must_not_do: treat more unstructured logs as observability
declare delivery healthy from worker process uptime
